content: 1. Administer 1 mg/m² of dronabinol orally once daily, 1 to 3 hours before chemotherapy, to reduce the risk of central nervous system (CNS) symptoms. Refer to adult dosing guidelines for titration. 2. Cefotetan increases the toxicity of dronabinol by inhibiting aldehyde dehydrogenase. This combination is contraindicated. Cefotetan contains 5% (w/w) propylene glycol, which can cause disulfiram-like reactions if coadministered with dronabinol. Discontinue cefotetan at least 14 days before starting dronabinol solution, and do not administer cefotetan within 7 days of completing dronabinol treatment. 3. Disulfiram increases the toxicity of dronabinol by inhibiting aldehyde dehydrogenase. This combination is contraindicated. Disulfiram also contains 5% (w/w) propylene glycol, which can cause disulfiram-like reactions if coadministered. Discontinue disulfiram at least 14 days before starting dronabinol solution, and do not administer disulfiram within 7 days of completing dronabinol treatment. 4. Metronidazole increases the toxicity of dronabinol by inhibiting aldehyde dehydrogenase. This combination is contraindicated. Metronidazole contains 5% (w/w) propylene glycol, which can cause disulfiram-like reactions if coadministered. Discontinue metronidazole at least 14 days before starting dronabinol solution, and do not administer metronidazole within 7 days of completing dronabinol treatment. 5. Tinidazole increases the toxicity of dronabinol by inhibiting aldehyde dehydrogenase. This combination is contraindicated. Tinidazole contains 5% (w/w) propylene glycol, which can cause disulfiram-like reactions if coadministered. Discontinue tinidazole at least 14 days before starting dronabinol solution, and do not administer tinidazole within 7 days of completing dronabinol treatment. 6. Apalutamide decreases the level or effect of dronabinol by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, can lower the exposure of drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates. If coadministration is unavoidable, evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect and adjust the dose as needed. 7. Danazol increases the level or effect of dronabinol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 8. Fexinidazole increases the level or effect of dronabinol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, which may increase the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. 9. Ivosidenib decreases the level or effect of dronabinol by inducing hepatic CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor patients for loss of therapeutic effect of CYP2C9 substrates. 10. Dronabinol and metoclopramide intranasal increase each other's effects through an unknown mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid metoclopramide intranasal or interacting drugs depending on their importance to the patient. 11. Nelfinavir increases the level or effect of dronabinol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 12. Dronabinol and olopatadine intranasal both increase sedation. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration increases the risk of CNS depression, leading to additive impairment of psychomotor performance and daytime impairment. 13. Ropeginterferon alfa-2b and dronabinol both increase neuropsychiatric side effects. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Narcotics, hypnotics, or sedatives can produce additive neuropsychiatric side effects. Monitor patients for excessive CNS toxicity if coadministered. 14. Tucatinib increases the level or effect of dronabinol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of CYP3A4 substrates according to product labeling. 15. Dronabinol and zuranolone increase each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration may increase impairment of psychomotor performance or CNS depressant effects. If unavoidable, consider dose reduction. 16. Alpelisib decreases the level or effect of dronabinol by inducing hepatic CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 17. Amiodarone increases the level or effect of dronabinol by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Dronabinol is a CYP2C9 substrate. 18. Amobarbital increases the level or effect of dronabinol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Dronabinol is a CYP3A4 substrate. 19. Dronabinol increases levels of amphotericin B cholesteryl sulfate by competing for plasma protein binding. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Dronabinol is highly bound to plasma proteins and may displace other highly protein-bound drugs, increasing their free fraction. Exercise caution with drugs that have a narrow therapeutic index. 20. Apalutamide decreases the level or effect of dronabinol by inducing hepatic CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration with CYP2C9 substrates may lower their exposure.
